sources.names.customs: Civil Code of Japan art. 750: a married couple take one surname, the husband's or the wife's by agreement. wife_takes_husband_bps 9500 is the figure given in the brief from the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare vital statistics (marriage statistics; about 94 to 95 percent of couples choose the husband's name) (to confirm: the table was not opened). Order family-first is Japanese usage (Family name, Given name). Children take the parents' shared surname (family_name_from father). Titles Mr/Ms: how English-language Japanese papers write them (the Japanese -san is not used); (to confirm).
sources.names.given: Opened: Meiji Yasuda Life Insurance, 'Birth-year ranking of names, top 10' (生まれ年別名前ベスト10), boys https://www.meijiyasuda.co.jp/enjoy/ranking/year_men/boy.html and girls .../girl.html, 1912 to 2025, from the company's policyholder data (page opened 2026-10-17; licence not stated on the page, all rights presumably reserved: only the ranks were read, summarised here as frequencies, not republished). Method: each year's top 10 gets 10..1 points (ties share the rank's points); years are summed per cohort (1930-44, 1945-59, 1960-74, 1975-89, 1990-99, 2000-09, 2010-19, 2020-25), so a weight is rank points not a count, and only names that reached the top 10 in some year appear (22 to 45 per cohort, fewer in the oldest/youngest). Spellings are kanji on the source; romaji is plain Hepburn without macrons using the commonest reading of each spelling (several kanji share a reading and merge; a few readings are ambiguous, e.g. Hinata/Yota, Haru; chosen by hand, to confirm). Birth years before 1930 are not used. Only frequencies are used: a drawn name may coincide with a living person by chance.
sources.names.family: Opened: namaeranking.com, Akita Prefecture surname ranking (秋田県の名字ランキング), ranks 1 to 99 with head-counts (https://namaeranking.com/ , page opened 2026-10-17; the page does not state its underlying data or licence: PLACEHOLDER as to provenance, to confirm). sources.names.institutions: Generic types of Japanese local bodies at town level, carrying the town's name: Town of {town} (the municipality, Local Autonomy Act); credit union (shinkin bank type); a registry office of the Legal Affairs Bureau (real-estate registration is kept by it); a summary court (Courts Act: disputes under 1.4 million yen, including rent claims; possession suits go to summary or district court, and civil conciliation may come first); administrative counselling (Gyosei Sodan; Japan has no general ombudsman); consumer affairs centre (Consumer Administration Act); election administration commission (Public Offices Election Act); police station of the prefectural police; waterworks department (Waterworks Act); municipal clinic; municipal elementary and junior high school; pension office of the Japan Pension Service. A hand-made choice, not a source list; none of these names is a real body. (to confirm)

sources.culture.conducts: What people start out holding right, for the four conducts where a figure in this profile's own outlook speaks to it (the rest start from values alone: no figure was opened). approves_bps is the national share with 'a great deal' or 'quite a lot' of confidence, as `outlook.trust` has it (World Values Survey and European Values Study, joint wave 7, as Our World in Data publishes it; opened 2026-10-11, to confirm against the survey's tables; see sources.outlook for the country and the items). Mapping, ours: answer_tribunal and take_to_tribunal <- confidence in the courts (a person who trusts the courts approves of answering a case there and of taking a wrong to it); complain <- confidence in the civil service (writing to the town is approved where the town's officers are trusted to answer); join_union <- confidence in labour unions. Weak: confidence in an institution is not approval of an act toward it, and the share above a threshold is read as a mean, as outlook does; the figure sets where people start (their own lean and their picture of what others approve), nothing else, and the lean is measured from it, so the rates stay the calibrated ones. No figure for strike, take_in, stay_past_notice, take_from_employer or an organisation's conduct (the survey's items on joining strikes and on the justifiability of stealing property were not opened); no figure by origin group (no source found that gives one). National, not the place's. does_bps is never given: a conduct's own rate in the profile.
sources.culture.origin: PLACE: Akita Prefecture (the prefecture, not Ikawa Town), nationality, end of 2024. groups: Immigration Services Agency, 'Number of foreign residents at the end of 2024' (Ministry of Justice), table 5 (by prefecture and nationality), https://www.moj.go.jp/isa/content/001434756.xlsx (from https://www.moj.go.jp/isa/publications/press/13_00052.html), OPENED 2026-10-13: Akita 5,851 foreign residents: China 939, Viet Nam 1,086, Korea 470, Philippines 1,011, other 2,345. Population 897,000 on 2024-10-01 (Statistics Bureau, population estimates, seen in a search result about Akita Prefecture, NOT opened: to confirm). Japanese nationals are 897,000 less 5,851 (so the shares are about 0.65% foreign in all; the estimate includes foreign residents). Shares in basis points, rounded; Japan takes the remainder. same_household_bps: 9660 (to confirm) = 100% less 3.4%, the share of marriages in Japan where one spouse is a foreign national (2016, from a search result on the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare vital statistics, NOT opened; IPSS table https://www.ipss.go.jp/syoushika/tohkei/Data/Popular2022/T06-17.files/sheet001.htm was opened but unreadable). National, not Akita. homophily_bps: PLACEHOLDER 5000 (a close tie is half again as likely within a group as by chance). No survey of close ties or friendship by group for this place was found and opened; McPherson, Smith-Lovin and Cook 2001 ('Birds of a feather', Annual Review of Sociology 27) gives the general fact, not this place's figure. CHILDREN: nationality follows the parents (a child of a mixed couple is a Japanese national if either parent is, which would put it in the Japan group; Nationality Act, from memory, to confirm); the generator's equal-chance rule would put half of such children among foreign nationals, so it does not fit well.
sources.tenancy.rent_share_of_income: PLACEHOLDER: no distribution, median or mean of rent against income was found (the Housing and Land Survey 2023 has renting households by income class and rent in e-Stat tables 115-1 and 48-1-1, which were not readable; mean rents read: Japan 59,656 yen a month, Akita 42,004). The bands are borrowed from de-ni-2026's (Lower Saxony's, of net income): another place of regulated tenancies and public housing, and no more than that. HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/generator.md, "Homes by income"): each renting household of a new town draws its share from these bands (evenly within a band; the open band from its lower bound to twice it, at most everything), which gives the rent it carries; households and let homes are matched by it. A target as well: the town's own distribution at the start is reported beside it and is not fitted to it.
sources.support.take_up_bps: pension 91.7%: DERIVED from opened figures: recipients of the basic old-age pension aged 65 and over, summed by single year of age (MHLW, overview of the employees' and national pension schemes, fiscal 2023), over the population aged 65 and over (36.25 million, Statistics Bureau, September 2024); national (opened 2026-10-12). The payment for those out of work is reckoned from a record of contributions and opens with nobody drawing it (about 24% of the unemployed drew it in fiscal 2023: 423 thousand recipients a month over 1.78 million unemployed, derived; recorded, not used). HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/generator.md, "Payments in force"): of those the payment's rule already entitles as the year begins, this share open with it in payment; the rest claim it when they first look, as before.
sources.ownership.owner_bps_by_age: Statistics Bureau of Japan, Housing and Land Survey 2023, table 45-1-1 (tenure by age of the household's main earner), national (opened 2026-10-12): owner households 13.8% under 35, 49.9% at 35-44, 62.2% at 45-54, 70.6% at 55-64, 80.8% at 65 and over (60.9% overall; Akita 77.1% overall, no split by age found). sources.tenancy.possession: PLACEHOLDERS: Japanese courts end a lease for unpaid rent only where trust between the parties has broken down, commonly about three months' arrears (case law under the Act on Land and House Leases and the Civil Code: recalled, to confirm); the rest are placeholders. Eviction is by a court execution officer, for whom the police stand. The two shares of how tenants answer are the same in every profile: stay_past_notice_bps 5000 is a PLACEHOLDER (no figure was found for the share of tenants who stay past a notice for arrears); leave_on_order_bps 5900 is England's, used everywhere: of 16,848 landlord possession orders in January to March 2026, 6,888 repossessions were by county court bailiffs, 41%, so about 59% of those ordered out were gone without one (Ministry of Justice, Mortgage and Landlord Possession Statistics, January to March 2026: opened by a research agent for this work, 2026-10-11; a ratio of one quarter's flows, not of one cohort). eviction_notice_days: the notice of the day that whoever carries out a warrant gives the tenant; England's county court bailiffs give 14 days' notice of an eviction (Civil Procedure Rules 83.8A: to confirm, recalled), Germany's Gerichtsvollzieher about three weeks (to confirm); every other place's figure is a PLACEHOLDER (7 days; Ohio 3, within its ten). HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/justice.md, "Possession"): published in the town as a law; a landlord gives a notice to vacate under it, applies to the tribunal if the tenant stays, and asks for a warrant if they stay past its order; the tribunal sets a plan or a date by it; the police carry the warrant out. Tenants who answer, and plans (2026-10-12): answer_bps 4000 is a PLACEHOLDER (no figure was found for this place of how many tenants served with an application for possession answer it in writing or attend; it is the middle of the two figures opened for other places: 43% of hearings with the renter or someone for them in Victoria, 39.3% of tenants present in Cleveland, Ohio). plan_consider 'may' is a PLACEHOLDER: possession cases commonly end in a settlement in court to pay by instalments (wakai: recalled, to confirm).
sources.business.entry_bps_per_year: Small and Medium Enterprise Agency, White Paper on SMEs 2025, from employment insurance records: opening rate 3.9% of establishments in FY2023, closing rate 3.9% (to confirm: read from a search summary). National; Akita's own not retrieved. It counts establishments that employ, so it understates businesses of one. HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/entry.md, "Starting a business of one"): the generator turns it into a monthly chance for those who could start a business of one (in the labour force, of working age, with the savings for its stock), from the businesses the town has: births a year at this rate, over those people. Most real births are businesses with no employees, which is the only kind that can be started here without premises.
sources.employment.hours: Labour Standards Act art. 26 (opened at japaneselawtranslation.go.jp, 2026-10-13): for an absence from work for reasons attributable to the employer, the employer pays an allowance of at least 60% of the average wage; art. 32 (40 hours a week; recalled). A real change of hours also rests on the contract or reasonable work rules (Labour Contract Act; to confirm); here the cut is taken as the employer's stand-down, with no spell limit. The Employment Adjustment Subsidy that refunds the employer about two thirds (small firms) is not modelled (to confirm; not opened). HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Hours before heads"): published in the town as a law (law-cutting-hours); a shop or factory over its need cuts everyone's hours to what its trade needs before it lets anyone go, where this says it may, and pays what it owes for the hours cut; a worker reads the employer's paper as the pay agreed. consent_bps 9000 is a PLACEHOLDER (of workers asked to agree to a cut as the alternative to someone being let go, the share who do; no figure found). The employer's own notice of 3 days is ours, so that the paper reaches the worker first. 2026-10-16: Labour Standards Act art 26 (at least 60% of the average wage for an absence the employer causes) is as in the note; the Employment Adjustment Subsidy (two thirds of the allowance for small firms, search summary) is not modelled.
sources.employment.adjustment: PLACEHOLDERS, the same in every profile, with a sourced shape (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Adjusting labour"; docs/research/references.md). smooth_months 3: firms plan production and workforce on smoothed, forecast trade and not on the last period's (Holt, Modigliani, Muth and Simon 1960); no figure for the horizon of a small employer here was found. hiring_cost_weeks 8: what recruiting and training a new worker costs, in weeks of their pay; estimates run from under two weeks to over sixteen (Silva and Toledo 2009; Manning 2011; Blatter, Muehlemann and Schenker 2012; Muehlemann and Leiser 2018: all to confirm, none opened), and none is for this place.
sources.employment.termination: Labour Standards Act art. 20 (30 days' notice or 30 days' average wages in lieu); no statutory severance pay (set by a firm's work rules, left out). The courts' four-factor test for redundancy dismissals, which makes them rare, is not a figure and is not modelled: firms here will shed more readily than Japan's do (to confirm: recalled by a research agent for this work, 2026-10-11, the statute not opened). HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Adjusting labour"): published in the town as a law; an employer reads it before letting someone go for redundancy (what it would owe is part of what the job costs to end) and pays what it says when the job ends. Service is counted from the start of a run: nobody's earlier years with an employer are known to it.
sources.frictions: Everyday frictions (docs/behaviour/frictions.md): what goes wrong, how often, and how the bodies that hear it work. Read by the generator only for a town whose spec has `living`.
sources.frictions.per_adult_bps_per_year: Of adults, the share who had each kind of problem, a year: half the share who had it in the last two years in World Justice Project, Global Insights on Access to Justice 2019 (General Population Poll 2017-18, about 1,000 respondents a country; the summary statistics workbook was opened; national, and for Brazil and Mexico the three largest cities only). landlord: a problem with a landlord over agreements, payments, repairs, deposits or eviction (1.4% in two years; all of it is given to disrepair here, which overstates repairs: the town has no other landlord problem of the kind yet). wages: difficulty obtaining wages or employment benefits agreed in advance (1.0%). bill: major disruption of a utility's supply or incorrect billing (1.3%; all of it is given to wrong bills). benefits: difficulty obtaining public benefits or government assistance (1.2%). goods: a consumer problem (4.0%) less the utility share, since the survey's consumer problems include it (derived; poor professional services are in it too). The generator turns each into a rate for those exposed (a let dwelling, a job, a customer, a claim) with the town's own counts. Halving a two-year share understates a yearly one where people have a problem in both years (to confirm against a yearly survey). 2026-10-16 (not applied): labour standards offices dealt with 22,354 wage non-payment cases in 2024, 185,197 workers, about 17.2 billion yen claimed (Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, https://www.mhlw.go.jp/bunya/roudoukijun/chingin-c_r06.html, opened, text partly garbled; 2023: 21,349 cases, 181,903 workers, 10.19 billion yen, press summaries), about 30 basis points of the roughly 60 million employees a year: the same order as the 50 here, but an enforcement caseload and not a prevalence; the sum per worker (56,000 to 93,000 yen) is over unpaid periods and cannot give a share of pay, so pay_short_by_bps 500 stays. Retail electricity and gas consultations (PIO-NET, FY2024: 4,514 and 530, https://www.kokusen.go.jp/soudan_topics/data/electricity_gas.html) give volumes, not a share of wrong bills. A legal-needs survey cited in a search result (about 19% of adults with a legal problem in five years, 3.8% a year) is consistent in magnitude with the 380 basis points summed here.
sources.frictions.put_right_on_asking_bps: Asked to put it right, how often the other side does. PLACEHOLDERS, every one: each stands at the share of people with any problem who say it is done and fully resolved (46.0%: World Justice Project, Global Insights on Access to Justice 2019 (General Population Poll 2017-18, about 1,000 respondents a country; the summary statistics workbook was opened; national, and for Brazil and Mexico the three largest cities only)), which is an outcome of everything people tried, not the rate at which the other side agrees when asked: to replace with a figure by kind of problem.

sources.frictions.support: (Until foundations F6 this note also gave a processing time, a placeholder fortnight, and a daily capacity; both are gone: how long a claim takes is the hours of whoever decides it.) wrong_refusal_bps: of claims that qualify, the share wrongly refused. FITTED in the 1,000-person town of the first profile (7% of qualifying claims gives about as many refusals a year as 6% of adults, its survey share with difficulty obtaining public benefits, counting the refusals that are right), and for every other place scaled by its own survey share against that one: a stand-in until a place's own rate of decisions changed on review is found. 2026-10-12: this fit assumed every entitled person claims in the year. Reviews of payments in force, which would add wrong stops, were looked for in this place's law and statistics and no rate of wrong stops per review was found; nothing is built (docs/behaviour/frictions.md, 'Payments in force are not reviewed'; docs/decisions.md, 2026-10-12, 'Reviews of payments in force'). 2026-10-16: no appeal or overturn rate for the livelihood-protection decisions was readable (MHLW welfare administration report, MIC appeal surveys: PDFs unreadable); 70 stays a stand-in.

sources.outlook: How people start out in what they trust (docs/behaviour/citizen.md, 'The record'). National figures for Japan, not the region's: none by region was found. trust: the share with 'a great deal' or 'quite a lot' of confidence in each kind of institution (`government`, `policing`: the police, `courts`, the civil service, banks, the press, labour unions, churches or religious organisations, major companies); people_bps: the share who say most people can be trusted. World Values Survey and European Values Study, joint wave 7 (fieldwork 2017 to 2022), as Our World in Data publishes it (ourworldindata.org/grapher/trust-state-institutions-wvs, trust-organizations-wvs, self-reported-trust-attitudes), opened 2026-10-11 through a tool that returns a page's figures in summary: to confirm against the survey's own tables. The share is read as the mean level of trust a person starts with, which is a simplification (a share above a threshold is not a mean). Not stated, so the citizen's own placeholders apply (to source: the survey's question on freedom of choice and control over one's life, its mean and spread, needs the microdata): how much control over their lives people feel (outlook.agency).
sources.outlook.residence: PLACEHOLDER: no figure for how long people have lived at their address was found for Japan on a page opened. Borrowed from Australia's (the only place whose figures were opened), for lack of any: ABS, 2021 Census, 'Population movement in Australia' (released 8 November 2022; abs.gov.au/articles/population-movement-australia), opened 2026-10-11: 53.1% of the population lived at the same address five years before the Census; 14.3% changed address within Australia in the year before; 0.7% had lived overseas a year before. Bands here: under 1 year = 14.3 + 0.7 = 15.0%; 1 to under 5 = the rest (31.9%); 5 and over = 53.1%. They are built from the one-year and five-year mobility rates, so the 1 to under 5 band is the remainder, and the 5-and-over share is the share at the same address five years earlier (population aged 5 and over, not adults only). National figures, not Victoria's: the Victoria figures were not found on an opened page. The open band is read as 5 to 15 years by the generator. Japan's own are probably different (to source: Census or housing-survey tables of years since moving in).
sources.outlook.job_tenure: How long employed people have been with their current employer (starting attachment to the trade). OECD, 'Employment by job tenure intervals' (dataset OECD.ELS.SAE DSD_TENURE@DF_TENURE_FREQ, measure TENURE_EMP, share of employment by time with the current employer; both sexes, all ages), national figures for Japan, 2025; read from the OECD SDMX API (sdmx.oecd.org/public/rest/data/OECD.ELS.SAE,DSD_TENURE@DF_TENURE_FREQ) on 2026-10-11, the response opened and the figures copied: under 1 year, 1 to under 3, 3 to under 5, 5 to under 10, 10 and over. National, not the region's: none by region was found. It covers the employed (employees and the self-employed), where a person's tenure is the time in the present job. The open band (10 and over) is read as 10 to 30 years by the generator. The shares sum to 99.9 to 100 in the source and are scaled to 10000.
sources.currency: Japanese yen: ISO 4217 JPY, no minor unit (0 decimal places; the sen is not in use, so an amount is a whole number of yen and money is counted in yen). Written with the yen sign before the amount (¥1,234) or in words as yen (the word is the same in singular and plural). Currency Act 1987 (Japan), art. 2: the yen is the unit; amounts are written in whole yen.  (Act and ISO 4217 from memory; to confirm.) How its people write money: the yen sign before the digits with no space, commas between thousands (no decimals in use). Unicode CLDR (cldr-json, cldr-numbers-full/main/ja/numbers.json, opened 2026-10-08): decimal '.', group ',', currency pattern '¤#,##0.00'. Japanese also counts in myriads (man, 10,000; oku, 100,000,000); no source for how these are written in English text was opened, so no number_words are set. Both marks are stated.

sources.wages_per_pay_period: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, Basic Survey on Wage Structure 2024 (Reiwa 6), Akita results as published by the Akita Labour Bureau, 'Akita Wage Statistics' (Nov 2025), https://jsite.mhlw.go.jp/akita-roudoukyoku/content/contents/002492552.pdf, tables 3-1, 3-3, 3-4 (establishments of 10 or more employees), read 2026-10-08. Monthly scheduled cash earnings (thousand yen) and annual bonus (thousand yen), men / women: manufacturing 270.4 / 194.0 and 801.4 / 432.9; construction 291.0 / 232.4 and 636.2 / 568.1; wholesale and retail 277.6 / 197.4 and 722.7 / 362.8. Fortnightly pay = (12 x monthly scheduled earnings + annual bonus) / 26, weighting men and women by assumed employment shares (manufacturing 70% men, construction 90% men, retail 50%): the weights are my assumptions, not published figures. Overtime is excluded. These are the industries' average full-time-type pay, not minimums; Akita's minimum wage is 1,031 yen an hour from 31 March 2026 (same document, annex 3; about 82,500 yen a fortnight at 80 hours). PAY PERIOD GAP: Japanese employees are paid monthly, not fortnightly; the figure is the monthly pay scaled to a fortnight.

sources.retirement_age: Basic old-age pension age 65 (National Pension Act; claiming can be deferred to 75). Employers must secure work to 65 (Act on Stabilization of Employment of Elderly Persons). STRUCTURAL GAP: Japan has no single retirement age; about half of 65-69 year olds work (Labour Force Survey), which a single retirement age cannot show. Statutory facts from memory; to confirm. Since 2026-10-08 people here stop work at ages of their own, drawn from labour_force_share_by_age; this age is still the one the profile's other figures turn on (the retired's savings, the end of the payments for those out of work, a retirement fund's access) and the top of the working ages the measures use. The pension's age is the payment's own (support.payments).
sources.savings_by_age: An adult's cash and deposits, 10th/25th/50th/75th/90th percentiles by age. The 50th percentiles are set from the median financial assets of households of two or more people by age of head, 2024: 20s 840,000 yen, 30s 1.8 million, 40s 2.5 million, 50s 2.5 million (the 55+ band is raised towards the 60s' 6.5 million), 60s 6.5 million, 70s 12.05 million (Financial Services Agency-affiliated J-FLEC, Survey of Household Financial Behaviour, 2024, two-or-more-person households, https://j-flec.go.jp/wpimages/uploads/yoronf24.pdf; figures as reported in a search summary, the PDF not opened: to confirm). They are household, not individual, holdings and include non-holders. The other percentiles and the 18-24 band are PLACEHOLDERS.
sources.retiree_savings: Median financial assets of two-or-more-person households headed by people in their 60s (6.5 million yen) and 70s (12.05 million yen), J-FLEC, Survey of Household Financial Behaviour 2024 (as for savings_by_age; to confirm); used as the range.
sources.support.payments: [The pension:] Basic old-age pension (National Pension), full monthly amount FY2026: 70,608 yen (up 1.9% from 69,308), Japan Pension Service notice, https://www.nenkin.go.jp/oshirase/taisetu/kojin/2026/202604/0401.html (read 2026-10-08). Paid every second month for the two preceding months (the 15th of even months), so 141,216 yen every 61 days (365/6 = 60.8). from_age 65. Left out: the earnings-related employees' pension that most Akita retirees with an employment history also receive (average well above the basic pension), contribution-record reductions, means-tested welfare (seikatsu hogo) and the couples' rate. STRUCTURAL GAP: a second, earnings-related tier. [The payment to those out of work:] Employment Insurance basic allowance (Employment Insurance Act). Opened: Hello Work, Basic allowance (https://www.hellowork.mhlw.go.jp/insurance/insurance_basicbenefit.html, opened 2026-10-08): the daily amount is about 50-80% of the previous daily wage (45-80% at 60-64), the more the lower the wage; upper limits per day from 1 Aug 2024: under 30, 7,450 yen; 30-44, 8,270; 45-59, 9,110; 60-64, 7,830; benefit days run from 90 to 360 by age, insured period and reason for leaving. The page did not give the lower limit or the 28-day cycle (I am recalling that benefits are recognised and paid in four-week cycles; to confirm). The flat figure is DERIVED: 60% (my choice inside the 50-80% range) of a daily wage of about 7,900 yen (the Akita retail monthly scheduled earnings of 237,500 yen, from the wage survey above, over 30 days) = 4,740 yen a day, x 28 days = 132,700 yen. from_age 18. STRUCTURAL GAP: contribution requirement, wage-linked amount, limited duration. SHAPE (2026-10-08, track D of docs/design/profile-depth.md): support is now a list of payments, each a rule in three parts: who qualifies, how much, for how long (docs/behaviour/boundary.md); the law is published and the payments office reads it. The payments for those out of work end the year before the profile's retirement age (to_age): the rule the generator applied to every profile until now, written into the payment, where it can be changed. The pension is as it was (every 61 days). UN-FOLDED: the flat allowance, which the author derived as 60% of a typical daily wage for 28 days, is now that rule itself: 60% (the author's choice within the law's 50 to 80%) of the claimant's own previous pay for 28 days, no more than the daily upper limit for their age times 28 (7,450 yen under 30; 8,270 at 30 to 44; 9,110 at 45 to 59; 7,830 at 60 to 64, as this note gives them), for those with contributions on the insurance's record, paid from employees' social insurance. Nobody has a record on the first day of a run, so those out of work at the start are paid nothing until they have worked. Not set: how long it lasts (this note gives a range, 90 to 360 days by age, insured time and why the job ended, and no table: the field is `lasts.days`), the insured time needed (`who.record.months`), the lower limit (`amount.least`), the rate rising for the low paid.

National Labour Force Survey, August 2026, opened: employment rate 80.3% for ages 15-64 and 62.5% for those 15 and over; unemployment 2.5% (Statistics Bureau of Japan, Labour Force Survey (Basic Tabulation), August 2026, https://www.stat.go.jp/data/roudou/sokuhou/tsuki/pdf/gaiyou.pdf, opened 2026-10-08). sources.labour_force_share_by_age: ILOSTAT, 'Labour force participation rate by sex and age (%)', five-year bands (dataflow DF_EAP_DWAP_SEX_AGE_RT, https://sdmx.ilo.org/rest/data/ILO,DF_EAP_DWAP_SEX_AGE_RT/all?startPeriod=2019; the data file opened and these figures read from it, 2026-10-08), persons, Japan, national, annual 2025, from the Statistics Bureau's Labour Force Survey: ages 25 to 54, 90.248%; 55 to 59, 85.9%; 60 to 64, 76.9%; 65 and over, 26.5%. National, not Akita (no table by age for the region was found); not checked against the Statistics Bureau's own table (to confirm). The note on retirement_age says about half of 65 to 69 year olds work; a search summary gives the 2025 survey's shares as 54.5% at 65 to 69, 36.2% at 70 to 74 and 12.6% at 75 and over (Statistics Bureau, topics no. 149; not opened: to confirm), which would split the open band. How it is used: the first band is the reference; someone in the labour force stops work at the start of a later band with the chance these shares give, and those still in at the last band never stop. The survey's last band is open (65 and over), so nobody is drawn to stop after 65, and those who work on are older on average than they are in fact: to split when the shares at 65 to 69, 70 to 74 and 75 and over are opened. The profile's own participation figure (labour_force_participation_bps) still says how many are in the labour force at the reference ages; this curve says only how that share falls with age.
sources.tenancy: Act on Land and House Leases (Shakuchi-shakuya-ho), arts. 26-28, 32: a lease renews unless the landlord gives notice 6 to 12 months ahead and has a justifiable cause; rent is changed by agreement, or by a court if the parties disagree (art. 32); there is no cap or notice period for an increase like some countries' rules. Custom: two-year leases, renewed with a renewal fee (so rent_review_months 24 and 30 days' notice are PLACEHOLDERS from custom). STRUCTURAL GAP: the 'justifiable cause' rule for ending a tenancy. After a fixed term the lease renews as a continuing one ('periodic'). From memory; to confirm.
sources.tenancy.end_notice_days: Act on Land and Building Leases (Shakuchi-shakuya-ho), arts 26 to 28 and 32 (https://www.japaneselawtranslation.go.jp/ja/laws/view/3787/en, opened 2026-10-16): a landlord's notice ending a lease of indefinite term takes effect six months after it is given (art 27), the landlord needs justifiable grounds (art 28), notice of non-renewal is given between one year and six months before the term ends (art 26). 180 days is the six months. The grounds' test is not modelled. Replaces the example code's 60 days.
sources.tenancy.tenant_notice_days: To confirm: a tenant's notice to end a tenancy of indefinite term takes effect three months after it is given, under the Civil Code (art 617, the text not opened; seen in a search summary of the Act's page, https://www.japaneselawtranslation.go.jp/ja/laws/view/3787/en, which was opened for the landlord's side). 90 days. sources.public_finance.income_tax: STATED AS PUBLISHED, National Tax Agency (opened 2026-10-08): income tax rates on taxable income, https://www.nta.go.jp/taxes/shiraberu/taxanswer/shotoku/2260.htm: up to 1.949 million yen 5%; 1.95-3.299 million 10% less 97,500; 3.3-6.949 million 20% less 427,500; 6.95-8.999 million 23% less 636,000; 9-17.999 million 33% less 1,536,000; 18-39.999 million 40% less 2,796,000; 40 million and over 45% less 4,796,000; plus a reconstruction special income tax of 2.1% of the tax (1.1% from 2027). Employment income deduction for 2026 and 2027, https://www.nta.go.jp/taxes/shiraberu/taxanswer/shotoku/1410.htm: 740,000 yen to 2.2 million of pay; 30% + 80,000 to 3.6 million; 20% + 440,000 to 6.6 million; 10% + 1,100,000 to 8.5 million; 1.95 million above. Basic deduction for 2026, https://www.nta.go.jp/taxes/shiraberu/taxanswer/shotoku/1199.htm (the page says it takes effect on 1 December 2026): 1.04 million yen at total income up to 1.32 million; 620,000 to 3.36 million; 680,000 to 4.89 million; 670,000 to 6.55 million; 620,000 to 23.5 million. Resident tax (prefectural 4% and municipal 6%, flat 10% of taxable income, basic deduction 430,000) and employee social insurance at 15% of pay are from memory (to confirm). THE APPROXIMATION, separately and mine: the structure takes marginal rates on gross annual pay. I computed total tax (national with the reconstruction tax, plus resident tax) on pay G as national tax on max(0, G - employment deduction - basic deduction - 15% of G) plus 10% of max(0, G - employment deduction - 430,000 - 15% of G), and fitted marginal rates between 1.38, 2.2, 3.6, 6.6, 8.5 and 13 million yen of pay: nothing up to 1.38 million, then 11.68%, 8.31%, 11.79%, 22.22%, 27.13% and 36.38% (above 13 million). The fit is within a few thousand yen of the computed tax at the nodes, and within about 7,000 to 20,000 yen between 2 and 5 million. Family deductions (spouse, dependants) and other deductions cannot be expressed. The 'levy' stands for employees' social insurance (health about 5%, long-term care 0.9% from 40, employees' pension 9.15%, employment insurance 0.55%, about 15.6%; from memory, to confirm) charged from 1.3 million yen; the 15% in the derivation above is deducted because insurance premiums are deductible from taxable income. SHAPE (2026-10-08, track E of docs/design/profile-depth.md): the law is now a list of charges, each with what it is charged on, its schedule, its reliefs and whom it is paid to (docs/behaviour/public-finance.md). The income tax and resident tax keep the author's fitted marginal rates on gross pay (the approximation described above; the deductions it folds could now be said as deductions, `base.less`, one of them a share of pay within a least and a most: left for the author). The levy of 15% of the whole of a pay from 1.3 million yen, which stood for employees' social insurance, is the same figure as a charge of its own, paid to the social insurance bodies and not to general revenue; its parts (health, long-term care, pension, employment insurance) are from the author's memory and sum to about 15.6%, so they are not split. The employers' report of it names each worker and their pay: the record the employment insurance payment is reckoned from.

sources.justice: Japan's equivalent is the summary court (small claims and civil disputes, up to 1.4 million yen) and district court, with the Labour Tribunal for wage disputes; rent disputes are rare in court. hearing_after_days 30: a first hearing about a month after filing (placeholder; the Supreme Court's civil case statistics give times to judgment, to source). pay_within_days, challenge_bps, apply_bps and apply_after_days are PLACEHOLDERS carried over. Enforcement of an unpaid money judgment by attachment of the debtor's bank account (Civil Execution Act).
sources.elections: Local Autonomy Act and Public Offices Election Act: mayors and assemblies are elected every four years; the mayor by a plurality in a direct vote, assembly members by a single non-transferable vote (modelled as a plurality); voting is not compulsory. turnout_bps 6,000: turnout in town and village elections in Japan is typically 60% or so, and mayoral elections in small towns higher (MIC, election results; recalled, to confirm). stand_bps and news_readers_bps: PLACEHOLDERS (Akita has high newspaper readership: the Akita Sakigake Shimpo; to source from the Japan Audit Bureau of Circulations or MIC).
sources.education: school_ages 6-17: nine years of compulsory schooling from age 6 (School Education Act) and about 99% go on to upper secondary school, which ends at 18 (MEXT, School Basic Survey; recalled, to confirm). students_per_teacher 11.0: PLACEHOLDER for a rural Akita public school (Japan's average is about 14-15, MEXT School Basic Survey 2024; Akita lower; not looked up). school_days_per_year 200 (MEXT: about 200-210 school days; recalled), hours_per_day 6 (placeholder). teacher_wage_per_pay_period 250,000 (about 6.5 million yen a year / 26; public school teachers, MIC local public servant pay survey, recalled, to confirm). attainment: PLACEHOLDER shares of adults by highest level of education, shaped by the Census 2020's education table for Akita (lower secondary only about 18%, upper secondary 48%, vocational or junior college 20%, university 14%: my recollection of the pattern, not read from the table; to replace from e-Stat), years of schooling 9, 12, 14, 16. return_per_year_bps: the wage return to a year of schooling, about 10% (the international literature, Psacharopoulos and Patrinos 2018; Japan's estimates are lower, 6-8%; to confirm), applied as productivity (Mincer 1974); max_years placeholder.

Landscape shares around the town: Akita is about 71% forest (Akita Prefecture forest statistics; recalled, to confirm) and about 10% farmland, but a town on a plain has more paddy around it: woodland 35%, scrub 5%, grassland 5%, farmland (mostly rice paddy) 45%, wetland 10% are PLACEHOLDERS. Covers' succession (cleared land to grassland in a year; scrub to woodland in about 40) and the pollution figures, survey_hours_per_ha, survey_staff and spin_up_years are placeholders carried over.
sources.nature.species: Three real species of Akita; ecology figures are PLACEHOLDERS except where stated. Japanese squirrel (Sciurus lis): males' home ranges 4-30 ha and females' 4-17 ha, litters of 2-6 after a 39-40 day gestation, IUCN Least Concern (Wikipedia, 'Japanese squirrel', https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_squirrel, opened 2026-10-08; a secondary source citing field studies, not checked against them). Home range set at 10 ha (the middle of those ranges); density 0.15 a hectare is DERIVED from it (about one adult per 10 ha, with some overlap between sexes), not an observed density. Black-spotted pond frog (Pelophylax nigromaculatus): clutch 1,800-3,000 eggs (600-5,000 by other estimates), maturity at about two years, maximum longevity about 13 years, IUCN Least Concern (Wikipedia, 'Dark-spotted frog', https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark-spotted_frog, opened 2026-10-08); breeds April-June in paddies, males holding territories on the water surface (Honda, species guide, https://www.honda.co.jp/outdoor/adventure/tonosamagaeru.html, via a search summary; to confirm). Density, home range, dispersal, mortality and pollution tolerance are placeholders. Japanese bush warbler (Horornis diphone; uguisu): a common songbird of scrub and woodland edge whose male song marks a territory in spring and summer (Canon bird-branch page, https://global.canon/ja/environment/bird-branch/photo-gallery/uguisu/, via a search summary; to confirm). The only research paper the English Wikipedia article cites is Hamao and Hayama 2015 on the Ogasawara Islands population (Ornithological Science 14: 111-115), which is an introduced population, so not used; densities and territory size are placeholders. TRIED AND NOT READ: the Ecosystem Conservation Society - Japan habitat-suitability sheets for the squirrel and warbler (https://www.ecosys.or.jp/certification/jhep/img/model/nihonrisu.pdf, uguisu.pdf): the PDFs' text is garbled, no numbers could be extracted. Listing: the Ministry of the Environment Red List status of the frog and squirrel was not confirmed, so neither is marked listed. Growth, mortality, dispersal, min_viable and detection: placeholders; family groups sharing a home range are not modelled.
sources.automation: (PB-6) The outside world's offers of systems to businesses (docs/behaviour/automation.md). Prices are those of vendors in US dollars, converted at an approximate 2026 rate of 150 JPY to the dollar (to confirm; the rate is not the place's own and is not read by any code), into the currency's smallest unit; they are the outside world's, held at today's level unless a yearly change is given, like world prices. self-service-point: a bank of self-checkout or self-ordering units: set-up about US$15,000 (a unit's list price runs US$15,000 to 25,000 installed in retail trade reports; to confirm), a yearly licence and support about 16% of it (support contracts run 10 to 20% of the hardware; to confirm), three years' licence, US$3,000 to leave. It does a share of the task 'serve' (scope: placeholder, 30%, in the range of the share of a retail worker's tasks that Eloundou, Manning, Mishkin and Rock 2023 find exposed to current systems; to confirm) in as long as a person takes (placeholder). production-cell: an automated line or cell: set-up about US$90,000 for a cell (the installed cost of an industrial robot system is a few times the robot's price of about US$50,000: International Federation of Robotics, World Robotics; to confirm), a yearly licence and maintenance about 10% of it, five years' licence, a fifth of the set-up to leave; it does 35% of the task 'make' (placeholder) in 70% of a person's time (placeholder). oversight_hours_per_month and error_bps are placeholders (what looking after one costs the buyer's own staff; how often it gets a unit wrong, refunded at the unit's price). case-handling-system: a system that writes an office's routine papers (a rates notice, a permit decision) and records them: set-up about US$40,000 and a yearly licence of 30% of it (a public-sector case-management system's price; placeholder, to source), three years' licence, a fifth of the set-up to leave; it writes them in 15% of a clerk's time (placeholder) and can do 60% of them (placeholder, in the range Eloundou et al. 2023 give for clerical work; to confirm). Mistakes: 2% of papers (placeholder; automated administration's error rates are a documented risk: Michigan's Auditor General found most fraud determinations of its unemployment system wrong, 2016 (to confirm)).
sources.automation.price_fall_bps_per_year: 0: the outside world's prices for systems are held at today's level (the default); a scenario (worlds/scenarios/falling-system-prices.yaml) gives a yearly fall, with its basis.
sources.automation.firms: (PB-6) How a business weighs a system (docs/behaviour/automation.md). payback_months: the months over which the costs of changing (set-up, exit) must be repaid, 24 for a small business and 36 for a large one (ten staff or more): placeholders, in the range firms report requiring for equipment of two to three years (Graham and Harvey 2001, 'The theory and practice of corporate finance', Journal of Financial Economics; to confirm). hurdle_bps: the margin by which the saving must beat the cost, 20% (placeholder, a margin of safety for a manager's own estimate being unsure). reference_bps: each business already using it that the vendor names eases the hurdle by 2 points, never below nothing (Mansfield 1961, 'Technical change and the rate of imitation', Econometrica; Griliches 1957; Rogers 2003: uptake follows how many have taken it up; the size is a placeholder). on_cost_bps: what staff cost beyond their wage, 0: the world models no employer's charges beyond the wage and redundancy pay. most: the most systems of one kind it takes at once (placeholder).
